subject: Post-demo follow-up: data handling, DPA items and evidence
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Chen <sasha.chen@dataworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — data handling & DPA questions

Hi Sasha,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and the open items we committed to follow up on for DataWorks: 

1) Data residency: You flagged that EU customer records must remain in the EU by default. We can pin model serving and storage to eu-central-1 for those accounts — confirm whether you need hard residency for backups/logs as well.

2) PII scope: We discussed separating three tiers (Identifiers, Sensitive attributes, and Derived model outputs). Please confirm a sample field list you consider PII so we can map it to our retention policies.

3) Retention & logs: You asked for default retention periods and whether audit logs (request/response metadata, not model outputs) can be retained for 90 days vs. 365 days. We can supply a configurable retention policy; need to know your minimum/maximum.

4) Subprocessors & DPA: You requested the current subprocessors list and breach-notify timing. Attached is our current DPA draft and a brief SOC2 summary; I’ve highlighted the subprocessor disclosure section.

5) Breach notification: We discussed SLA for notification to customer security contacts and whether 48 hours is acceptable for the initial notification. Please indicate if you require a different window or a custom communication flow.

Next steps I propose:
- You/Legal Ops confirm residency scope (data + backups + logs) and retention windows for PII and logs.
- If you share a short list of fields you consider PII, we’ll return a mapped matrix showing where/how each field is stored and the recommended retention.
- Marissa (legal) can run through any suggested DPA edits; Rishi (privacy engineering) will validate audit-log options and retention configuration.

If you’d prefer, we can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow with Legal and Privacy to resolve the outstanding items and align on a timeline for an updated DPA.

Attachments: DPA-draft-v1.pdf (redline-ready), SOC2-summary-stub.pdf

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sasha Chen <sasha.chen@dataworks.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@dataworks.com>
Date: 2025-09-04T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — data handling & DPA questions

Thanks Mateo — good recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: DataWorks requires EU residency for any EU citizen customer records, including backups, snapshots, and logs that can be linked back to individuals. That means both primary store and backups must be in-region.

- PII fields: I’ll attach a short CSV with the fields, but for now assume: name, email, phone, national_id, address, DOB, and any health-related attributes are considered PII.

- Retention: Our baseline is 7 years for records with regulatory relevance, but for request/response logs (audit trail) we prefer 1 year. Can Redwood support distinct retention for model inputs/outputs vs. system logs?

- Subprocessors: We need a complete current list and a commitment to notify us within 14 days for new subprocessors and to provide a way to review high-risk subprocessors.

- Breach notify: Our legal team requires initial notification within 48 hours of detection and a detailed incident report within 10 business days. Is Redwood able to commit to that window in the DPA?

Also looped in Legal Ops (legal@dataworks.com) — they may push back on some DPA language. Please include Marissa and Rishi on any contract edits.

Thanks,
Sasha Chen
Head of Product Security, DataWorks Inc

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Chen <sasha.chen@dataworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Legal Ops <legal@dataworks.com>
Date: 2025-09-05T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — data handling & DPA questions

Hi Sasha / DataWorks Legal Ops,

Appreciate the clear bullets — that helps. Quick responses below and proposed next steps.

- Residency: Confirmed — we can pin EU tenant data, backups, and snapshots to eu-central-1. We will include a clause in the addendum to require Redwood to maintain EU-only storage for designated tenants.

- PII mapping: Please share the CSV when convenient. Rishi will prepare a field-to-storage mapping and recommend retention zones (EU store, ephemeral compute, transient cache).

- Retention: Redwood supports configurable retention windows. Default we offer: model inputs/outputs: 30 days (can be extended), request metadata/audit logs: 365 days. We can commit to a one-year audit log retention for DataWorks if that is required; longer retention (7 years) for regulated records will need contract-side exceptions and we’ll propose a plan for archival storage in-region.

- Subprocessors: Current subprocessors list is included in the DPA draft (see attached). We typically notify customers of new subprocessors 30 days prior; we can align to a 14-day notification for DataWorks as a contract carveout, and offer an option to review high-risk subprocessors via a gated process (summary + security attestation).

- Breach notification: We can commit to initial notification within 48 hours of detection and a follow-up incident report within 10 business days. We’ll include those timeboxes in the DPA addendum.

Attachments: DPA-addendum-v1.1.pdf (contains EU residency clause, 14-day subprocessor notify commitment, and 48-hour initial notify SLA). Also re-attached SOC2-summary-stub.pdf for quick review.

Proposed next steps:
- Sasha / Legal Ops: review DPA-addendum-v1.1 and flag any redlines.
- Marissa: if you can take the primary legal touchpoint, I’ll coordinate a short call (30 mins) for Friday to finalize language.
- Rishi: will draft the field-to-storage matrix once Sasha shares the CSV sample.

If that works, I’ll schedule the call and send a DocuSign link for the addendum once you’ve agreed to edits.

Best regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123
